harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) to permit and log TCP/23 traffic from node3 to node4, and node2 (OPNsense) to reject and log that same traffic, using a forced routing path (node3 → node1 → node2; the four nodes actually share one flat /24, so node2 would otherwise route straight to node4). A live connection attempt from node3 produced one correlated log-entry pair — same IP ID, source port, and destination port — showing accept-and-log at node1 immediately followed by block/reject-and-log at node2, proving traffic was permitted through node1 and stopped at node2. All four nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol; boot-identity changes were confirmed on every node, and the routing/firewall configuration and the pass/refuse behavior were verified to persist and reproduce identically after all four reboots.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 4 nodes: node1=VyOS, node2=OPNsense, node3/node4=RHEL10, all sharing one flat /24 (10.100.84.0/24) with a common platform gateway
On node3: added a persistent NetworkManager static route (10.100.84.13/32 via 10.100.84.10) so traffic destined for node4 is forced through node1 first

On node1 (VyOS): set protocols static route 10.100.84.13/32 next-hop 10.100.84.11 (forces onward hop to node2) plus firewall ipv4 forward filter rule 10 (action accept, log enabled, protocol tcp, destination port 23, source 10.100.84.12, destination 10.100.84.13); committed and saved

On node2 (OPNsense): edited /conf/config.xml to add a reject filter rule (quick, log enabled) on interface lan for tcp/23 from 10.100.84.12 to 10.100.84.13, then ran configctl filter reload; verified via pfctl -s rules as 'block return ... log quick ... port = telnet'

Triggered a TCP connect attempt from node3 to node4:23 via a python3 socket (received Connection refused), then pulled the matching accept-log line from node1 (nftables kernel log, prefix ipv4-FWD-filter-10-A) and the matching block-log line from node2 (pflog JSON), sharing identical IP ID, source port, and destination port — proving the same packet was permitted at node1 and refused at node2
Captured pre-restart baselines on all 4 nodes: boot_id/kern.boottime, uptime, and confirmation the firewall rules/routes were active

Restarted node1 via backgrounded reboot, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed and the forward-filter accept+log rule for tcp/23 was still present with reset packet counters
Restarted node2 via backgrounded reboot, polled until exec was available again, confirmed kern.boottime changed and the reject+log pf rule was still present
Restarted node3 via backgrounded systemctl reboot, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed and the static route to node4 via node1 persisted
Restarted node4 via backgrounded systemctl reboot, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed

Re-ran the end-to-end connection attempt from node3 after all four restarts and re-captured a fresh correlated log pair (matching IP ID 53104, source port 58322, destination port 23) from node1 (accept) and node2 (block), confirming full post-restart recovery of the required behavior

evidence.requirement: node1 permits and logs node3->node4 tcp/23 traffic
evidence.summary: VyOS forward-filter rule 10 committed with action accept, log enabled, matching src 10.100.84.12/dst 10.100.84.13 tcp/23; nft ruleset shows the compiled accept+log rule with nonzero packet counter after traffic passed

evidence.requirement: node2 refuses and logs the same traffic
evidence.summary: OPNsense config.xml reject rule added and reloaded; pfctl -s rules confirms compiled rule 'block return in log quick ... from 10.100.84.12 to 10.100.84.13 port = telnet'; filter log directory located at /var/log/filter/

evidence.requirement: single attempt from node3 produces a correlated pair of log entries showing where traffic stopped
evidence.summary: python3 socket connect from node3 to node4:23 returned Connection refused; node1 kernel log shows accept for SRC=10.100.84.12 DST=10.100.84.13 ID=10887 SPT=39468 DPT=23 SYN; node2 pflog shows block for the identical packet (same ID/SPT/DPT/flags), proving traffic passed node1 and was stopped at node2

evidence.requirement: node1 baseline health and boot identity, restart, changed identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 9d3cb897...; backgrounded reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id 73e0caa4... (changed) with fresh uptime; forward-filter accept+log rule for tcp/23 confirmed present after reboot with reset counters

evidence.requirement: node2 baseline health and boot identity, restart, changed identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime Jun 14 2026; backgrounded reboot acknowledged; post-reboot kern.boottime Sep 6 2026 (changed); reject+log pf rule confirmed present via pfctl after reboot

evidence.requirement: node3 baseline health and boot identity, restart, changed identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 368725cb...; backgrounded systemctl reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id d003c76b... (changed); static route to node4 via node1 confirmed persisted via NetworkManager

evidence.requirement: node4 baseline health and boot identity, restart, changed identity
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 2db46909...; backgrounded systemctl reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 963d9afd... (changed), confirming node4 restarted

evidence.requirement: post-restart end-to-end re-verification of the permit/refuse log pair
evidence.summary: After all four reboots, a fresh connection attempt from node3 again returned Connection refused; node1 logged accept and node2 logged block for the same packet (matching ID 53104, SPT 58322, DPT 23), confirming the behavior and configuration fully recovered post-restart
